standard.title: Elastomer Insulated Flexible Cables for Use in Mines — Specification (First Revision)
standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements, construction types, testing schedules, and sampling criteria for flexible elastomer-insulated cables designed for power transmission, control, lighting, and auxiliary systems in coal mines, quarries, and other underground or surface mining operations [1, 2]. It covers cables operating at rated voltage grades of 1.1 kV, 3.3 kV, 3.8/6.6 kV, and 6.35/11 kV [1].

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under Quality Control Orders (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers and the Electrotechnical Department of the Government of India, all mining cables manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 14494 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial electrotechnical cables, as it is strictly reserved for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.
requirements: Every cable drum or attached label must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L).
Cables rated at 1.1 kV and 3.3 kV grades are suitable for both earthed and unearthed electrical networks, whereas 3.8/6.6 kV cables are specifically suitable for earthed 6.6 kV systems.

It is permissible to split the earth conductor into equal parts and lay them in the outer interstices. Split-up earth conductors must have the same colour or number code to maintain traceability and core identification.

For rated voltages above 6.6 kV (E), power cores must feature a conductor screen consisting of extruded semi-conducting compound applied over a semi-conducting tape. Conductor screening is not required for pilot and earth cores.
Multi-core cables must be easily identified using a distinct colour scheme: a) 2 Cores: Power core is Red, Earth core is Green; b) 3 Cores: Power core is Red, Pilot core is Black.

Cables are classified into functional types to ensure safety under specialized mining conditions: a) FT1: 3-phase intrinsically safe cables for U/G production systems requiring infrequent movement; b) P3: Power feeders for transport and ventilation systems; c) FT3: Power cables for heavy mobile production machinery; d) PLC2 to PLC5: Cables for lighting and auxiliary control circuits.

To prevent mechanical crushing and shear forces during mobile mining, core layouts such as Cable Type P3 or PA1 must feature insulated power, pilot, and earth cores laid around an elastomeric cradle separator.

Cables with rated voltages above 3.3 kV must undergo partial discharge testing. The discharge magnitude at a test voltage of 1.73 Uo must not exceed 10 pC for routine/acceptance testing and must not exceed 5 pC for type testing.

To ensure uniform sheath and armour thicknesses across all manufacturers, dimensions are calculated using a fictitious diameter formula (e.g. Dc = dL + 2ti + 3.0 mm for screened cores) that ignores the shape and compaction of conductors.

The size and structure of steel strands in pliable armour must comply with Table 38 based on fictitious diameter under the armour: a) Up to 25 mm: 7/0.45 mm strand size; b) 25 to 40 mm: 7/0.70 mm; c) 40 to 60 mm: 7/0.90 mm; d) Above 60 mm: 7/1.25 mm.

The nominal outer sheath thickness must correlate with calculated fictitious diameters as per Table 37: a) Up to 10 mm: 2.5 mm; b) 10 to 15 mm: 2.8 mm; c) 25 to 30 mm: 4.0 mm; d) 40 to 50 mm: 5.0 mm; e) 50 to 60 mm: 5.7 mm; f) Above 100 mm: 9.0 mm.
Each consignment lot (consisting of same-sized cables produced under identical conditions) must be randomly sampled and tested per Annex F to verify conformity before delivery.
